items.title: Australia 'very concerned' by Chinese ballistic missile test in Pacific
items.description: China has test-fired a long-range missile with a dummy warhead in the Pacific Ocean. The ABC has been told the Chinese government informed governments in the region about the test.

items.title: Socceroos winger says One Nation monoculture debate 'bulls***'
items.description: The Socceroos star says anyone "trying to divide" the community is "probably not Australian themselves".

items.title: Concerns about cricket pitches on ovals after Melbourne football tragedy
items.description: Nathan Fitzgerald's club has asked authorities to look at the way hard cricket pitches are covered on multi-use ovals as the 27-year-old continues to receive end-of-life care.

items.title: NSW government announces review into boy's death amid cannibalism probe
items.description: Cannibalism will form part of an investigation into the death of a four-year-old boy on the NSW Central Coast, with an independent review to take place by the Department of Communities and Justice.

items.title: 'Terrifying' roadside assistance ordeal sparks national change
items.description: A woman's campaign for change after her own frightening experience being broken down outside Canberra will see NRMA roadside assistance contractors required to provide a code to customers to verify their identity.

items.title: England's Azteca thriller a stunning deliverance from ghosts of the past
items.description: England teams of old would have buckled under the pressure put upon them by Mexico and their 80,000-strong band of supporters at the Azteca. But this England team turned a nightmare into a dreamland, at a venue haunted by so many ghosts of the past.

items.title: 'Assassination plot' impeachment trial involving Duterte dynasty begins in Manila
items.description: A highly consequential impeachment trial against Philippines Vice-President Sara Duterte could spell the end for her political career and shape the nation's 2028 election.

items.title: Australia enters new alliance with Fiji and more Pacific nations could join
items.description: Australia and Fiji strike a new defence alliance in a major development that could reshape the Pacific's strategic landscape.

items.title: 'Like a small iceberg': Rare whale calf spotted swimming off east coast
items.description: The calf, thought to be one of only a dozen in the Southern Hemisphere, has been spotted swimming alongside its mother.

items.title: The world is getting pure Trump and the US presidency may never be the same
items.description: Donald Trump is undertaking regime change, not just in Venezuela, but on US soil and it is unlikely the presidency will ever be the same.

items.title: More hateful content remains on Meta platforms after changes to moderation
items.description: A Meta executive has downplayed claims a change in the company's policies led to a rise in antisemitism while giving evidence to the royal commission.

items.title: This Place: Thaaklatjika Mingkana
items.description: Mutawintji National Park is an area rich in Aboriginal culture, painting and wildlife, and where the red desert is now green and lush. As part of NAIDOC Week the ABC is looking at Indigenous peoples' connection to country, and what makes it so special. NAIDOC Week is marking 50 years of Deadly and runs from July 5 until July 12.

items.title: Council demands illegally cleared Sydney land be restored despite secret sale
items.description: In 2020, Amir Abu Abara illegally cleared land in Barden Ridge to build a lavish mansion. After a fine, a replanting works order, and the rejection of his housing plan, he is no longer the site's owner.

items.title: PM apologises for saying he would 'shag' Kylie Minogue in podcast game
items.description: Anthony Albanese made the comments during a game of "shag, marry, date" on the Bush Deep podcast on Friday, which have been widely condemned as inappropriate.

items.title: How the beloved bin chicken became a video game inspiration
items.description: As part of NAIDOC Week, we meet the Indigenous creatives who are re-shaping Australia's video game industry.

items.title: Love a self-saucing pudding? These four are delicious and easy
items.description: You'd never guess it but self-saucing puddings are so easy to make. Here are four of our best for you try while the weather is cool.

items.title: Is a full day of screen time for kids ever OK?
items.description: Screen time has become a phrase that makes "parents feel instantly guilty", but how detrimental is a full day of screens on the odd occasion, like during school holidays or when you are home sick?

items.title: 'Pink army' Thunderbirds fans flock to Rundle Mall
items.description: Hundreds of fans have flocked to Rundle Mall, dressed in pink, to welcome back the Adelaide Thunderbirds following an unforgettable grand final win.

items.title: Reporting on Venezuela's disaster when we heard: 'Call your embassy right now'
items.description: Instead of focusing all its efforts on coordinating a widescale rescue operation, the Venezuelan government has been accused of hindering the response, and as has become apparent, our ability to cover it.

items.title: The yellow blocks creating a 'game of cat and mouse' in Gaza
items.description: The "Yellow Line" that marks the boundary of Israeli-controlled territory in Gaza has been moved deeper into the enclave.

items.title: Neil the Seal is 1 tonne right now. What happens when he's 4 tonnes?
items.description: The elephant seal has been attracting onlookers in southern Tasmania as well as a growing social media audience. But fears for his wellbeing, and concerns that some people aren't keeping their distance, have led to calls to better protect Neil.

items.title: Nigel Farage referred to watchdog over 'gifts' from crypto investor 'Posh George'
items.description: Nigel Farage was reportedly provided with security services, social media support and accommodation by George Cottrell, a 32-year-old crypto investor who previously served eight months in prison for wire fraud.

items.title: Live: ASX retreats amid takeover battle for miner as oil price falls
items.description: The ASX is down in afternoon trade, despite the Gulf ceasefire holding and a positive sentiment on global markets. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: 'Oldest continually practised medicine' being passed on to students
items.description: Aboriginal Australians have used native plants as bush medicine for tens of thousands of years. On Larrakia land, medical students are learning how nature can heal.

items.title: Billions in cash can't be accounted for. Where is it all going?
items.description: There is no shortage of theories, from stacks of cash hidden at home to illicit activities, but little in the way of definitive answers.
